subject.title: [Bug]: Slack replies ~2s slower than other channels — dominant cost is Socket Mode event delivery; channel-side stalls fixed in #101888

question: Should Slack latency be resolved by adding stronger HTTP Request URL guidance for hosted public-ingress deployments, or should OpenClaw change Slack setup/default behavior beyond the existing `mode: "http"` support?
rationale: HTTP mode already exists, but stronger setup/default changes would alter operator expectations, credential requirements, and public-ingress assumptions for Slack deployments.

options.title: Document HTTP latency guidance
options.body: Keep Socket Mode as the default for local/private deployments and update Slack docs/setup guidance to prefer HTTP Request URLs for hosted public-ingress deployments where reply latency matters.

options.title: Change setup or defaults
options.body: Sponsor a broader setup/default change that steers new hosted Slack installs toward HTTP mode, with upgrade and operator guidance.

options.title: Accept current guidance
options.body: Decide the existing transport table is sufficient and close only after recording that no additional latency-specific docs or setup change is planned.

recommendation.title: Document HTTP latency guidance
recommendation.body: Keep Socket Mode as the default for local/private deployments and update Slack docs/setup guidance to prefer HTTP Request URLs for hosted public-ingress deployments where reply latency matters.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the measurement context and the merged partial Slack latency fix, making them the best current routing candidate for the specific HTTP-guidance decision.
